question:
Two congruent squares, \(ABCD\) and \(PQRS,\) have side length \(15.\) They overlap to form the \(15\) by \(25\) rectangle \(AQRD\) shown. What percent of the area of rectangle \(AQRD\) is shaded?

[Figure 1](figures/2011_AMC_8_Q13_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The shaded region \(PBCS\) is the overlap of the two squares. Adding the squares' widths counts this overlap twice, whereas the rectangle's width counts it once. Thus the overlap's width is
\[
15+15-25=5.
\]
Its height is \(15\), so its area is \(5\cdot15=75\). The entire rectangle has area \(25\cdot15=375\).

The shaded fraction of the rectangle is therefore
\[
\frac{75}{375}=\frac15=\frac{20}{100}=20\%.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{20\%}\) is shaded, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
